 # Chapter 5: Grammar Representation and Loading
 
 ## 5.1 Overview
 
 This chapter covers how grammars are represented in LibGLR and how to load them from various sources. Topics include:
 
 - Grammar file formats
 - Building grammars programmatically
 - Parse table generation
 - Grammar validation
 
 ## 5.2 Grammar File Format
 
 LibGLR supports a Yacc/Bison-like grammar format:
 
 ```
 %token NUMBER PLUS MINUS TIMES DIVIDE LPAREN RPAREN
 %start expr
 
 %%
 
 expr : expr PLUS term
      | expr MINUS term
      | term
      ;
 
 term : term TIMES factor
      | term DIVIDE factor
      | factor
      ;
 
 factor : NUMBER
        | LPAREN expr RPAREN
        ;
 ```
 
 ### 5.2.1 Sections
 
 **Declarations section** (`%token`, `%start`):
 - `%token`: Declares terminal symbols
 - `%start`: Specifies the start symbol
 - `%left`, `%right`, `%nonassoc`: Declare operator precedence and associativity
 
 **Rules section** (after `%%`):
 - Production rules in BNF notation
 - `|` separates alternatives
 - `;` terminates a rule
 
 ## 5.3 Loading Grammars from Files
 
 ```c
 #include <glr/grammar.h>
 
 glr_grammar_t *grammar = glr_grammar_load("expr.grammar");
 if (!grammar) {
     fprintf(stderr, "Failed to load grammar\n");
     return 1;
 }
 ```
 
 The loader parses the grammar file and constructs the internal representation.
 
 ## 5.4 Building Grammars Programmatically
 
 For embedded grammars or dynamic generation:
 
 ```c
 glr_grammar_t *grammar = glr_grammar_create();
 
 // Add terminals
 int NUMBER = glr_grammar_add_symbol(grammar, GLR_SYMBOL_TERMINAL, "NUMBER");
 int PLUS = glr_grammar_add_symbol(grammar, GLR_SYMBOL_TERMINAL, "+");
 
 // Add non-terminals
 int expr = glr_grammar_add_symbol(grammar, GLR_SYMBOL_NONTERMINAL, "expr");
 int term = glr_grammar_add_symbol(grammar, GLR_SYMBOL_NONTERMINAL, "term");
 
 // Add productions
 glr_symbol_t *expr_sym = glr_grammar_get_symbol(grammar, expr);
 glr_symbol_t *term_sym = glr_grammar_get_symbol(grammar, term);
 glr_symbol_t *plus_sym = glr_grammar_get_symbol(grammar, PLUS);
 
 glr_symbol_t *body[] = {expr_sym, plus_sym, term_sym};
 glr_grammar_add_production(grammar, expr, body, 3);
 
 // Set start symbol
 glr_grammar_set_start_symbol(grammar, expr);
 ```
 
 ## 5.5 Parse Table Generation
 
 Parse tables are typically generated by external tools. LibGLR provides an API to attach precomputed tables:
 
 ```c
 glr_parse_table_t *table = generate_lr_table(grammar);
 glr_grammar_set_parse_table(grammar, table, true); // true = grammar owns table
 ```
 
 ### 5.5.1 Parse Table Structure
 
 From `include/glr/parsetbl.h`:
 
 ```c
 typedef struct {
     glr_state_t *states;      // Array of parser states
     size_t state_count;       // Number of states
     size_t terminal_count;    // Total number of terminals
     size_t nonterminal_count; // Total number of nonterminals
 } glr_parse_table_t;
 
 typedef struct {
     glr_action_set_t *action_table; // ACTION table (indexed by terminal ID)
     size_t terminal_count;          // Number of terminals
     glr_goto_t *gotos;              // GOTO table entries
     size_t goto_count;              // Number of GOTO entries
     size_t goto_capacity;           // Allocated capacity
 } glr_state_t;
 
 typedef struct {
     glr_action_t *actions;  // Dynamic array of actions
     size_t action_count;    // Number of valid actions
     size_t capacity;        // Allocated capacity
 } glr_action_set_t;
 ```
 
 ### 5.5.2 Building a Parse Table
 
 ```c
 glr_parse_table_t *build_parse_table(glr_grammar_t *grammar) {
     glr_parse_table_t *table = malloc(sizeof(glr_parse_table_t));
     
     // Compute LR(0) or LR(1) items
     // Build canonical collection of item sets
     // Compute ACTION and GOTO tables
     
     table->state_count = num_states;
     table->states = malloc(num_states * sizeof(glr_state_t));
     
     for (size_t i = 0; i < num_states; i++) {
         glr_state_t *state = &table->states[i];
         state->action_table = malloc(terminal_count * sizeof(glr_action_set_t));
         state->terminal_count = terminal_count;
         
         // Fill ACTION table
         for (size_t t = 0; t < terminal_count; t++) {
             glr_action_set_t *action_set = &state->action_table[t];
             action_set->actions = NULL;
             action_set->action_count = 0;
             action_set->capacity = 0;
             
             // Add shift/reduce/accept actions
             add_action(action_set, action);
         }
         
         // Fill GOTO table
         state->gotos = malloc(goto_count * sizeof(glr_goto_t));
         state->goto_count = goto_count;
     }
     
     return table;
 }
 ```
 
 ## 5.6 Grammar Validation
 
 Before using a grammar, validate it:
 
 ```c
 bool validate_grammar(glr_grammar_t *grammar) {
     // Check that start symbol is defined
     if (!grammar->start_symbol) {
         fprintf(stderr, "No start symbol defined\n");
         return false;
     }
     
     // Check that all productions have valid heads
     for (size_t i = 0; i < grammar->production_count; i++) {
         glr_production_t *prod = grammar->productions[i];
         if (!prod->head || prod->head->type != GLR_SYMBOL_NONTERMINAL) {
             fprintf(stderr, "Production %zu has invalid head\n", i);
             return false;
         }
     }
     
     // Check for undefined symbols in production bodies
     for (size_t i = 0; i < grammar->production_count; i++) {
         glr_production_t *prod = grammar->productions[i];
         for (size_t j = 0; j < prod->body_length; j++) {
             if (!prod->body[j]) {
                 fprintf(stderr, "Production %zu has undefined symbol at position %zu\n", i, j);
                 return false;
             }
         }
     }
     
     return true;
 }
 ```
 
 ## 5.7 Grammar Introspection
 
 Query grammar properties:
 
 ```c
 // Get all productions for a non-terminal
 void get_productions_for_symbol(glr_grammar_t *grammar, int symbol_id) {
     for (size_t i = 0; i < grammar->production_count; i++) {
         glr_production_t *prod = grammar->productions[i];
         if (prod->head->id == symbol_id) {
             printf("Production %zu: ", i);
             print_production(prod);
         }
     }
 }
 
 // Check if grammar is left-recursive
 bool is_left_recursive(glr_grammar_t *grammar, int symbol_id) {
     for (size_t i = 0; i < grammar->production_count; i++) {
         glr_production_t *prod = grammar->productions[i];
         if (prod->head->id == symbol_id && 
             prod->body_length > 0 && 
             prod->body[0]->id == symbol_id) {
             return true;
         }
     }
     return false;
 }
 ```
 
 ## 5.8 Example: Complete Grammar Setup
 
 ```c
 #include <glr/glr.h>
 
 int main(void) {
     // Load grammar from file
     glr_grammar_t *grammar = glr_grammar_load("c.grammar");
     if (!grammar) {
         fprintf(stderr, "Failed to load grammar\n");
         return 1;
     }
     
     // Validate
     if (!validate_grammar(grammar)) {
         fprintf(stderr, "Grammar validation failed\n");
         glr_grammar_destroy(grammar);
         return 1;
     }
     
     // Generate parse table
     glr_parse_table_t *table = generate_lr_table(grammar);
     if (!table) {
         fprintf(stderr, "Failed to generate parse table\n");
         glr_grammar_destroy(grammar);
         return 1;
     }
     
     // Attach table to grammar
     glr_grammar_set_parse_table(grammar, table, true);
     
     // Create parser
     glr_parser_t *parser = glr_parser_create(grammar);
     
     // Use parser...
     
     // Cleanup
     glr_parser_destroy(parser);
     glr_grammar_destroy(grammar); // Also destroys table
     
     return 0;
 }
 ```
 
 ## 5.9 Summary
 
 - Grammars can be loaded from files or built programmatically
 - Parse tables are generated externally and attached to grammars
 - Always validate grammars before use
 - Use introspection to query grammar properties
